coursework.en: Follow the assessment brief and course handbook: their requirements may restrict or prohibit AI use. General availability of a tool does not override them.
coursework.zh: 遵守考核任务书与课程手册，其要求可以限制或禁止 AI 使用；工具通常可用不能覆盖这些规定。

exams.en: Check the requirements for the specific assessment; the recorded general position does not grant blanket exam permission.
exams.zh: 请核对具体考核要求；已记录的一般立场不构成所有考试的一概许可。

disclosure.en: At submission, state whether AI was used. If it was, explain why, where and how, following the assessment’s requirements.
disclosure.zh: 提交时须说明是否使用 AI；如有使用，解释原因、使用位置及方式，并遵守该考核要求。

privacy_data.en: Do not enter protected data without the required prior IDG or Research Ethics approval. A Warwick-account Copilot recommendation is not that approval.
privacy_data.zh: 受保护数据未经要求的 IDG 或研究伦理事先批准，不得输入 AI；推荐使用 Warwick 账号的 Copilot 不等于已获批准。

approved_tools.en: Student guidance recommends Copilot chat with a Warwick account for relevant data, but access, data approval and assessment permission remain separate.

basis.evidenceSnippet: Regardless of costs, all new uses of AI tools and services/products or services, must go through appropriate procurement processes.
You will be required to state if any AI has been used as part of the submission procedure. If you use an AI, you must set out why, where and how you have done so.

The policy covers everyone who has a contractual (formal or informal/implied) relationship with the University, including employees, students, visiting academics, and consultants. The policy covers all information processed by the University, regardless of ownership or format.

Certain types of data must never be put into any AI software, without prior approval from IDG or the Research Ethics Committee. These include: Passwords and usernames. Personally identifiable information (PII) or other sensitive or confidential material. Any data related to University Intellectual Property.

The general position is that you can use Artificial Intelligence (AI) but must follow any requirements set out in assessments and course handbooks. Those requirements may restrict or prohibit the use of AI.
The principles set out in this guidance apply to all researchers as previously defined. Researchers must consider all risks that may be relevant to their research that arise from AI.

Do not input any personal or confidential data into any AI tools, unless you fully understand what will happen to that data. The university recommends using Co-Pilot chat for this kind of data - when logged in with your Warwick account.

Misconduct in research includes: the fabrication or falsification of research data; improper handling of information on individuals collected during research; or the use of another person's ideas, work or research data without appropriate acknowledgement. Researchers are responsible for any such practices, even if they occur inadvertently through the use of an AI tool.

use of generative AI technologies to produce text and other media as part of student submissions ... needs to be thoughtfully supported to ensure responsible use and clear demonstration of human achievements.

Responsible use includes ... using AI with honesty, in ethical and defensible ways, with human responsibility taken for the outcomes; being transparent about AI use; making concerted efforts to maximise safe and secure use; using AI in ways that mitigate bias and promote fairness, inclusivity and accessibility.

security_procurement.en: The Information Compliance Policy covers staff, students and others in scope; all new AI uses must follow appropriate procurement processes, regardless of cost.
security_procurement.zh: 信息合规政策涵盖其范围内的职工、学生等人员；所有新 AI 用途无论费用多少，都须经过适当采购流程。
security_procurement.meaningEn: Assessment briefs and course handbooks control student use; research, procurement and data approvals have their own scope. The Information Compliance Policy covers staff, students and others in scope; all new AI uses must follow appropriate procurement processes, regardless of cost.
security_procurement.meaningZh: 学生使用以考核任务书和课程手册为准；科研、采购及数据审批各有适用范围。 信息合规政策涵盖其范围内的职工、学生等人员；所有新 AI 用途无论费用多少，都须经过适当采购流程。

do.en: Follow the AI requirements in your assessment brief and course handbook.
do.zh: 遵守考核任务书和课程手册中的 AI 要求。

do.en: State whether you used AI and, if so, explain why, where and how at submission.
do.zh: 提交时说明是否使用 AI；如有使用，解释原因、使用位置及方式。

do.en: For a new AI use within the Information Compliance Policy, follow the appropriate procurement process even if the tool is free.
do.zh: 信息合规政策范围内的新 AI 用途，即使工具免费也须经过适当采购流程。

dont.en: Do not input the protected data categories in IMP02 without prior IDG or Research Ethics Committee approval.
dont.zh: IMP02 所列受保护数据，未经 IDG 或研究伦理委员会事先批准，不要输入 AI。

dont.en: Do not treat a Copilot recommendation as permission to ignore your assessment requirements.
dont.zh: 不要把 Copilot 推荐当作忽略考核要求的许可。

dont.en: In research, do not assume an AI tool removes your responsibility for unacknowledged use of others’ work or mishandled data.
dont.zh: 科研中，不要以为使用 AI 就免除了不当处理数据或未注明使用他人成果的责任。

scope.en: Assessment briefs and course handbooks control student use; research, procurement and data approvals have their own scope.
scope.zh: 学生使用以考核任务书和课程手册为准；科研、采购及数据审批各有适用范围。

claim-warwick-001.text: Warwick's student-facing guidance says students may use AI only within requirements set out in assessment briefs and course handbooks, which may restrict or prohibit AI use.
claim-warwick-001.scope: Follow the assessment brief and course handbook: their requirements may restrict or prohibit AI use. General availability of a tool does not override them.

evidence.quote: The general position is that you can use Artificial Intelligence (AI) but must follow any requirements set out in assessments and course handbooks. Those requirements may restrict or prohibit the use of AI.
evidence.location: Key principles for using AI / Check the rules

claim-warwick-002.text: Warwick's student-facing guidance says students are required to state whether AI was used in the submission process and explain why, where, and how it was used.
claim-warwick-002.scope: At submission, state whether AI was used. If it was, explain why, where and how, following the assessment’s requirements.

evidence.quote: You will be required to state if any AI has been used as part of the submission procedure. If you use an AI, you must set out why, where and how you have done so.
evidence.location: Key principles for using AI / Declare it

claim-warwick-010.text: Warwick's AI Information Compliance Policy says certain data, including personal or confidential material, University intellectual property, and some copyrighted or third-party data, must not be put into AI software without prior approval.
claim-warwick-010.scope: Do not enter protected data without the required prior IDG or Research Ethics approval. A Warwick-account Copilot recommendation is not that approval.

evidence.quote: Certain types of data must never be put into any AI software, without prior approval from IDG or the Research Ethics Committee. These include: Passwords and usernames. Personally identifiable information (PII) or other sensitive or confidential material. Any data related to University Intellectual Property.
evidence.location: Data restrictions

claim-warwick-003.text: Warwick's student-facing guidance tells students not to enter personal or confidential data into AI tools unless they understand what will happen to the data, and recommends Copilot chat with a Warwick account for that kind of data.
claim-warwick-003.scope: Do not enter protected data without the required prior IDG or Research Ethics approval. A Warwick-account Copilot recommendation is not that approval.

evidence.quote: Do not input any personal or confidential data into any AI tools, unless you fully understand what will happen to that data. The university recommends using Co-Pilot chat for this kind of data - when logged in with your Warwick account.
evidence.location: Key principles for using AI / Protect privacy

claim-warwick-005.text: Warwick's AI in research guidance says its principles apply to all researchers and researchers must consider AI-related research risks including integrity, information security, and accountability risks.
claim-warwick-005.scope: Research guidance requires researchers to consider AI-related risks and retain responsibility, including for misconduct arising inadvertently through a tool.

evidence.quote: The principles set out in this guidance apply to all researchers as previously defined. Researchers must consider all risks that may be relevant to their research that arise from AI.
evidence.location: Who is expected to use this guidance / Risk Considerations

claim-warwick-006.text: Warwick's AI in research guidance says researchers are responsible for misconduct-type practices involving AI, including improper handling of information or use of another person's ideas, even if such practices occur inadvertently through an AI tool.
claim-warwick-006.scope: Research guidance requires researchers to consider AI-related risks and retain responsibility, including for misconduct arising inadvertently through a tool.

evidence.quote: Misconduct in research includes: the fabrication or falsification of research data; improper handling of information on individuals collected during research; or the use of another person's ideas, work or research data without appropriate acknowledgement. Researchers are responsible for any such practices, even if they occur inadvertently through the use of an AI tool.
evidence.location: Breach of Responsibilities and Expected Standards

claim-warwick-004.text: Warwick's assessment-design guidance says generative AI use in student submissions needs thoughtful support so responsible use and clear demonstration of human achievement are maintained.
claim-warwick-004.scope: Assessment-design guidance calls for thoughtful support of AI-assisted submissions so human achievement remains clear; it is guidance for teaching design, not task permission.

evidence.quote: use of generative AI technologies to produce text and other media as part of student submissions ... needs to be thoughtfully supported to ensure responsible use and clear demonstration of human achievements.
evidence.location: Designing assessment for achievement and demonstration of learning outcomes

claim-warwick-008.text: Warwick's AI Information Compliance Policy covers everyone with a contractual or implied relationship with the University and all information processed by the University.
claim-warwick-008.scope: The Information Compliance Policy covers staff, students and others in scope; all new AI uses must follow appropriate procurement processes, regardless of cost.

evidence.quote: The policy covers everyone who has a contractual (formal or informal/implied) relationship with the University, including employees, students, visiting academics, and consultants. The policy covers all information processed by the University, regardless of ownership or format.
evidence.location: Scope and definitions

claim-warwick-009.text: Warwick's AI Information Compliance Policy says all new uses of AI tools, products, or services must go through appropriate procurement processes, regardless of cost.
claim-warwick-009.scope: The Information Compliance Policy covers staff, students and others in scope; all new AI uses must follow appropriate procurement processes, regardless of cost.

evidence.quote: Regardless of costs, all new uses of AI tools and services/products or services, must go through appropriate procurement processes.
evidence.location: Principles of the policy
